The '''Theed Royal Palace''', also known as '''Jewel of Naboo''', was the [[Monarch of Naboo|royalty's]] seat of power on the [[planet]] of [[Naboo]]. The palace was located in [[Theed]], the [[capital]] [[city]] of Naboo's [[human]] [[Naboo (people)|inhabitants]]. The palace's design was elegant and flowing, blending quite finely with the surrounding environment, and it connected to the [[Theed Hangar]] via several passages.

The palace's [[Throne room (Theed Royal Palace)|throne room]] was used for meetings between the monarch and the [[Naboo Royal Advisory Council]]. The [[throne]], which stood in front of a large [[Viewport|window]] in the room, also hid two [[blaster pistol]]s in a compartment, which was added in [[32 BBY]] by [[Eirtaé]] at the suggestion of [[Quarsh Panaka]]. The palace also had a hangar where several [[starship]]s were stored in case of emergencies.

==Description==
===Exterior and surrounding area===
[[File:TheedAttack.png|thumb|left|300px|The Palace Plaza terminated at the entrance to the Royal Palace.]]
Considered the loveliest building in [[Theed]], and thus the "Jewel of Naboo," the sprawling and baroque Theed Royal Palace was located in the [[city]] of Theed, [[capital]] of the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]] [[planet]] [[Naboo]]'s<ref name="Nexus" /> [[human]] [[Naboo (people)|inhabitants]],<ref name="explTPM">{{SW|url=films/star-wars-episode-i-the-phantom-menace|text=''Star Wars: The Phantom Menace''}}</ref> atop a plateau split by the [[Solleu River]] and the river's own [[Virdugo Plunge]]<ref name="SWE: Naboo">{{EncyclopediaCite|Naboo}}</ref> and between [[Palace Plaza]] and the [[Cliffs of Theed]]. Both ornate and ancient,<ref name="TRP Databank">{{Databank|theed-royal-palace|Theed Royal Palace}}</ref> its architectural style resembled that of the city around it,<ref name="SWCL" /> containing dozens of<ref name="Nexus" /> linked<ref name="SWE: Naboo" /> [[sandstone]] towers topped with bright [[Color|green]] domes trimmed with [[brass]].<ref name="Nexus" /> One such [[Veruna's tower|tower]], located near the back of the palace next to a skywalk, contained a library collection established by [[King]] [[Ars Veruna]] during his reign.<ref name="SWCL" />

The palace grew over time, as it was traditional for each new [[Monarch of Naboo|monarch]] of Naboo to construct a new tower or turret for the palace, an act for which they would then seek public acclaim.<ref name="SWCL" /> Over time, the streets and buildings of Theed were constructed to radiate outward with the palace as their center, further emphasizing its importance.<ref name="SWE: Naboo" /> The main entrance to the palace lay beyond four statues and a staircase,<ref name="Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]''</ref> and was often the ending point for any of the city's grand parades.<ref name="TRP Databank" /> A watchtower stood to the side of the building.<ref name="SWCL" /> A short ways away, the [[royal boathouse]] was located at the base of the cliffs.<ref name="Monster Misunderstanding">{{FOD|Monster Misunderstanding}}</ref>

[[File:Palace-Courtyard---original.png|thumb|right|300px|The Palace Courtyard, built from the ashes of the Trade Federation's invasion]]
A large and stately edifice, the Royal Palace dominated Theed and the surrounding area. The palace's importance was emphasized by the streets and buildings of Theed, which radiated from the structure. Nearby buildings were kept low-lying, and the main building was surrounded by parks and public spaces, allowing the structure to remain the focus of the city's skyline. The primary approach to the palace's entrance was the Palace Plaza, which terminated at a wide flight of steps leading to the principle portico of the Royal Palace itself.<ref name="SWE: Naboo" /> The plaza, stairs and portico served as the location for new monarchs' inauguration ceremonies and other major public events.<ref name="Queen's Shadow" /> The stairs were flanked by imposing statues of Naboo's foremost philosophers, artists, and historical leaders.<ref name="SWE: Naboo" /> Following the [[Invasion of Naboo]] by the [[Trade Federation]], a section of Theed adjacent to the palace that had been severely damaged during the invasion was replaced by the [[Palace Courtyard]], an enclosure that was designed to foster the principles of enlightenment.<ref name="SWCL" />

===Interior===
{{Quote|The difficulty is getting into the throne room. Once we're inside, we shouldn't have a problem.|Quarsh Panaka|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
[[File:Theed-Palace-Halls.png|thumb|left|300px|The halls of the palace were lined with towering columns.]]
The building's interior spaces were bright and airy, with tall, arched ceilings and many windows, giving even the smallest spaces a sense of openness.<ref name="Nexus" /> Several hallways were lined on each side with towering columns.<ref name="Episode I" />

The central interior space was the [[Throne room (Theed Royal Palace)|throne room]] and a meeting hall that was used for meetings between the monarch and the [[Naboo Royal Advisory Council]].<ref name="SWCL" /> A southwest hall, simply decorated except for large windows that took in a sweeping view of the city and its surroundings, was used for more informal gatherings. Other rooms included offices and quarters for the [[Naboo Palace Guard]], which was tasked with protecting the [[Monarchy|monarch]].<ref name="Queen's Shadow" />

Naboo's [[queen]]s used a suite on the fifth floor of the palace consisting of a dressing room with an extensive [[Clothing|wardrobe]] system attached, a sitting room, a small meeting room and three rooms for sleeping with one intended for the queen to use. The queen also had a [[Queen's library|private library]] down the hall from the royal apartments that was reserved for her use.<ref name="Queen's Peril" /> The Turret Room was located in a square tower near the back of the palace.<ref name="SWCL" /> Many rooms opened onto outdoor terraces and balconies.<ref name="Queen's Shadow" /> Within the palace were many disused chambers, secret rooms, and forgotten corridors.<ref name="Nexus" />

[[File:Theed_Main_Hangar.png|thumb|right|300px|The Royal Starport was relocated next to the Theed power generator, becoming the Theed Hangar.]]
Up until the development of the [[N-1 starfighter]], the caverns beneath the palace housed the [[Royal Starport]], used as a private facility by Naboo's rulers and volunteer security forces. With the N-1 requiring an uninterrupted power supply, the Royal Starport was relocated adjacent to the [[Theed power generator]] and became the [[Theed Hangar]],<ref name="SWE: Naboo" /> which was connected to the palace via a secret tunnel.<ref name="SWCL" /> The old starport then served as barracks for the palace guard and on-duty pilots.<ref name="SWE: Naboo" />

==History==
===Construction and the High Republic Era===
During the [[Great Time of Peace]] in [[832 BBY]], the Theed Royal Palace was constructed by the people of Theed alongside the Solleu River on the Cliffs of Theed under the direction of King [[Jafan]], who recently unified the Naboo and ended the [[Time of Suffering]].<ref name="Nexus" /> The palace eventually became the residence of King Ars Veruna, who ruled Naboo for thirteen years and oversaw the construction of Veruna's tower, which housed a large royal library established by Veruna.<ref name="SWCL" /> In [[382 BBY]],<ref name="Convergence Date">''[[Star Wars: The High Republic Character Encyclopedia]]'' dates the events of ''[[The High Republic: Convergence]]'' to [[382 BBY]].</ref> during the [[High Republic Era]], [[Jedi Knight]] [[Gella Nattai]] recognized an image of the palace on a screen that scrolled through galactic locations in a library on [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Orlen Mollo]]'s [[Longbeam-class corvette|Longbeam cruiser]] ''[[Paxion]]''.<ref name="Convergence">''[[The High Republic: Convergence]]''</ref>

Later throughout the [[Republic Era]], the palace continued to serve as home to Naboo's monarchs, many of whom added on towers to the structure. One such addition was the [[Overlook stage/Canon|Overlook stage]] constructed near the back of the palace, which was used to celebrate the Naboo holiday [[Festival of Light]] as a prominent fixture in the world's holiday schedule.<ref name="SWE: Naboo" />

===The reign of Padmé Amidala===
[[File:Naboo_Royal_Advisory_Council.png|thumb|left|350px|Queen Amidala, with her advisory council, in the throne room, at the Theed Palace.]]
In [[32 BBY]],<ref name="QP Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Queen's Peril]]'' to [[32 BBY]].</ref> shortly after [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]]'s [[Coronation of Queen Amidala|ascension]] as Queen of Naboo she told her head of security [[Quarsh Panaka]] that the only bodyguards she would have in her room were her [[Naboo Royal Handmaidens|handmaidens]]. To make up for this, Panaka added security measures into the room such as a [[weapon]]s cache in the [[Viewport|window]] seat which included a variety of things to help the Queen and several [[sensor]]s that could detect a perimeter breach, several more for various types of weapons discharge and [[Blood-sensitive sensor|one]] that would detect the presence of [[blood]], though Panaka's wife, [[Mariek Panaka]], demanded that he remove the blood sensor following an [[Period|incident]] with [[Saché]], the queen's youngest handmaiden.<ref name="Queen's Peril" />

Early into her reign, Amidala hosted a [[Chommell sector summit|summit]] at the palace with leaders of the other planets in the [[Chommell sector]] to improve relations, following the isolationist policies of Amidala's predecessor, Queen [[Sanandrassa]]. In the lead-up to the summit, Panaka put several measures of extra security in place, including a compartment in the centuries-old [[throne]] that could hide two [[blaster pistol]]s. This was done by the [[engineer]] [[Eirtaé]], one of Amidala's handmaidens, who made it so only the queen could open the compartment.<ref name="Queen's Peril" />

[[File:GunrayAmidalaBibbleTheedRoyalPalace-TPM.png|thumb|right|350px|B1 battle droids surround Amidala and her retinue as the Trade Federation takes over the Palace.]]
During the Trade Federation's occupation of the planet, the palace was seized and used as their base of operations, with Viceroy [[Nute Gunray]] and his senior staff holding it as their residence until forces led by Queen Amidala [[Battle of Naboo|assaulted]] it and captured Gunray. Later, [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], who had thought in the Battle of Naboo, was knighted by [[Yoda]] in the [[Turret Room]] inside the palace. There were also celebrations for the defeat of the Trade Federation on the palace stairs, where Amidala wore the [[Jubilation dress]] as she held the [[Globe of Peace]].<ref name="Episode I" />

[[File:StainedGlassHandmaiden.jpg|thumb|left|250px|One of the stain glass windows, depicting Amidala's handmaidens, wearing their flame-colored robes.]]
After the invasion, the wing leading to the Theed Hangar was sealed,<ref name="Shattered Empire 3">[[Shattered Empire 3|''Shattered Empire'' 3]]</ref> and, controversially, an [[ion pulse]] was installed in the palace<ref name="Queen's Shadow">''[[Queen's Shadow]]''</ref> as a precaution against further invasions. The system, powered by relays located throughout the city, disabled any electronic devices, including vehicles and weapons within its reach except those inside the palace.<ref name="Battlefront II" /> There were also several [[painting]]s and stained glass windows of Amidala's handmaidens wearing their [[flame-colored robes]] which were commissioned for the palace<ref name="Queen's Shadow" /> shortly after the invasion's end,<ref name="Queen's Hope">''[[Queen's Hope]]''</ref> including one with the handmaidens carrying a canopy over the queen.<ref name="Queen's Shadow" /><ref name="Battlefront II" /> The droid [[R2-D2]] kept a copy of the artwork in his memory and showed it to Amidala on at least one occasion, and the recognized the piece as from the Theed palace.<ref name="Queen's Hope" />

===Amidala's successors and the Clone Wars===
After Padmé's term as queen ended, the palace became the residence of her successor queen, [[Réillata]], who had also served a term as queen before Amidala's reign. Following her [[Second coronation of Réillata|second coronation]], Réillata entered the throne room with Amidala and the others where she asked Amidala to succeed [[Senator]] [[Oshadam]] as the Chommell sector's representative in the [[Galactic Senate]]. Amidala then retired to one of the palace rooms with her entourage where she decided to accept Réillata's. Amidala returned to the palace again, after her first full session in the senate, to talk with Réillata about her progress. Réillata also oversaw the final construction of the coin pulse.<ref name="Queen's Shadow" />

[[File:Jamillia-large.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The palace eventually became the residence of Queen Jamillia.]]
The palace would eventually become the residence of Queen [[Jamillia]].<ref name="Episode II">{{Film|II}}</ref> In [[22 BBY]],<ref name="SWGA">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> Amidala would once again return to the palace to speak with Jamillia and the [[Naboo Royal Advisory Council|Advisory Council]] regarding the [[Separatist Crisis]] and the looming threat of [[Clone Wars|war]].<ref name="Episode II" /> The same year,<ref name="QH Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Queen's Hope]]'' to [[22 BBY]].</ref> shortly after the [[First Battle of Geonosis]], Jamillia prepared to transition out of office, which would result in her not living at the palace. The handmaiden [[Dormé]] sent recommendation letters to the palace for several candidates she had interviewed to be one of Amidala's handmaidens, thinking the individuals would be better suited to life in the Theed court. Around this time, the handmaiden [[Sabé]] thought fondly of her time living in the palace as one of Amidala's handmaidens years prior, including when they had snuck out to see a [[Neurotransmitter Affection]] concert.<ref name="Queen's Hope" />

Not long after, Jamillia had been replaced by the noticeably younger Queen [[Neeyutnee]] who ruled during the Clone Wars<ref name="Databank">{{Databank|queen-neeyutnee|Queen Neeyutnee}}</ref> and moved fighter operations out of the palace.<ref name="Shattered Empire 3" /> At Neeyutnee's request, Padmé returned once more when the [[Raid on Nuvo Vindi's laboratory|presence]] of [[battle droid]]s was discovered on Naboo and later for the Festival of Light, an event which celebrated Naboo joining the [[Galactic Republic]].<ref name="Blue Shadow Virus">{{TCW|Blue Shadow Virus (episode)}}</ref><ref name="CON">{{TCW|Crisis on Naboo}}</ref> The festival took place in<ref name="CON" /> the Overlook stage<ref name="SWE: Naboo" /> of the palace courtyard under a [[ray shield]] and was the scene of an attempt to kidnap [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]]. Another [[Plan to kidnap Chancellor Palpatine|attempt]] was made by [[Count]] [[Dooku]] in the palace [[Theed Palace Banquet Hall/Canon|dining room]], but he retreated in failure after a [[Lightsaber duel|duel]] with Jedi Knight [[Anakin Skywalker]].<ref name="CON" /> Amidala occasionally thought of her time as queen in the palace, mentally picturing herself with her handmaidens there shortly prior to a [[Missiont to Clabron|mission]] to [[Clabron]].<ref name="AOR">[[Age of Republic - Padmé Amidala 1|''Age of Republic - Padmé Amidala'' 1]]</ref>

===The New Order===
Upon the [[Proclamation of the New Order|formation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]<ref name="ECUC">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]''</ref> in [[19 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> the queen at the time was [[Apailana]],<ref name="ECUC" /> who was eventually replaced by Queen [[Dalné]]. However, the position of Monarch of Naboo was almost entirely ceremonial, with the true power lying in the hands of [[Moff]] Quarsh Panaka. However, Panaka spent most of his time in his chalet on [[Onoam]], leaving Dalné in the palace.<ref name="Leia">''[[Leia, Princess of Alderaan]]''</ref> In [[3 BBY]],<ref name="LPOA date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Leia, Princess of Alderaan]]'' to [[3 BBY]].</ref> Dalné looked out her palace's windows and contemplated the world's moon, [[Onoam]]. She decided to depart the palace and travel to the moon, having little else to occupy her time by that point.<ref name="Leia webcomic">''[[Leia Organa: Ordeal of the Princess]]''</ref> Organa apologized to Dalné upon arrival, having assumed the queen would have remained in the Theed palace.<ref name="Leia" />

In [[3 ABY]],<ref name="Darth Vader 4 date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Darth Vader (2020) 4|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 4]] to [[3 ABY]].</ref> [[Sith Lord]] Darth Vader, who had once been Anakin Skywalker, flew past the Royal Palace in an [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|Imperial shuttle]] to [[Battle at Padmé's tomb|visit]] the [[Tomb of Padmé Amidala]], which the palace overlooked and could be seen from.<ref name="Darth Vader (2020) 4">[[Darth Vader (2020) 4|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 4]]</ref>

[[File:Theed.png|thumb|left|350px|Naboo celebrates the fall of the Empire.]]
After the [[Battle of Endor]] which marked the fall of the Empire, celebrations took place in the plaza in front of the palace. By this point,<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Shattered Empire 3|''Shattered Empire'' 3]] to [[4 ABY]]. Therefore [[Queen]] [[Sosha Soruna]] would been elected sometime during or prior to that [[Standard year|year]].</ref> Naboo was ruled by Queen [[Sosha Soruna]], who stayed at the palace with her entourage including her head of security [[Captain]] [[Korro]] and her handmaidens.<ref name="Shattered Empire 3" />

===The fall of the Empire===
Twenty days after the Battle of Endor, Soruna greeted [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] and her pilot, [[Shara Bey]], in the throne room where she offered her support to the [[New Republic]] that the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebellion]] was beginning to found. They were interrupted however when the Empire cut off their communications and Soruna had to open up the Theed Hanger, for the first time in over twenty years, using the Queen's Authority Override.<ref name="Shattered Empire 3" />

During the [[Battle of Theed]] against the Empire on Naboo, which was targeted by [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] Palpatine, who hailed from Naboo, as part of [[Operation: Cinder]], Rebel forces managed to activate the ion pulse and hold the palace. With the Imperials' weapons disabled and those of the rebels still functioning, the day was won by the Alliance.<ref name="Battlefront II" /> A picture of the palace was included in the Naboo section of the [[book]] ''[[Galactic Explorer's Guide]]'', [[author]]ed by the [[pirate]] [[Hondo Ohnaka]] and his [[RA-7 protocol droid|protocol droid]] [[DK-RA-43]] at some point after the [[Battle of Crait]]<ref name="Explorer's Guide">''[[Star Wars: The Galactic Explorer's Guide]]''</ref> in [[34 ABY]].<ref name="Timelines" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Conception for ''The Phantom Menace''===
[[File:NabooRoyalPalace-TPMP.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Concept art of the Theed Royal Palace by Doug Chiang]]
The Theed Royal Palace first appeared in the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="Episode I" /> For the film, artists [[Doug Chiang]], [[Ed Natividad|Edwin Natividad]], and [[Jay Shuster]] worked on production painting and storyboards for the palace, while [[Brian Flora]] created a matte painting of the palace and plaza. The final conceptual design of the palace facade was done by [[Kurt Kaufman]], and a foam core conceptual model of Theed, including the palace, was created by [[Ellen Lee]]. Concept art of the giant statues flanking the entrance of the palace was done by Natividad and was intended to make the figures appear made from marble and approximately 100 feet tall.<ref name="Art of TPM">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]''</ref>

[[File:MarinCivic-BlueMosque-CasertaPalace.png|thumb|left|300px|The Palazzo Reale (top left) was used as the palace interior, and the Marin County Civic Center (bottom left) and Blue Mosque (right) served as inspiration for the palace's exterior.]]
The [[Wikipedia:Italian Renaissance|Italian Renaissance]]-inspired<ref name="Galactic Backpacking 2">{{SW|url=news/galactic-backpacking-part-2-visiting-real-world-naboo|text=Galactic Backpacking, Part 2: Visiting Real-World Naboo|nolive=1}}</ref> design of Theed gradually evolved into a city paradise under the direction of [[George Lucas]], filled with flourishing gardens and flowing rivers. The desired blend of real-world aesthetics emerged after months of studying [[Wikipedia:Moorish architecture|Moorish]], [[Wikipedia:Architecture of Italy|Italian]], [[Wikipedia:Moroccan architecture|Moroccan]], and [[Wikipedia:Architecture of Turkey|Turkish]] architecture. Working alongside producer [[Rick McCallum]], production designer [[Gavin Bocquet]] was tasked with searching for a building that could serve as the inspiration for the city's palace. In [[1997]], the [[Caserta Palace|Palazzo Reale]] of [[Wikipedia:Caserta|Caserta]], [[Wikipedia:Italy|Italy]], became the interior of the film's palace. The [[Wikipedia:Baroque|baroque]]-[[Wikipedia:Rococo|rococo]] structure, built in [[Wikipedia:1752|1752]] to emulate [[Wikipedia:Versailles|Versailles]], fit in seamlessly with the design work of the art department for the film, its interior matching Theed's strength and splendor, along with its light sense of beauty and amiability. For the palace's throne room, Natividad experimented with various shapes and materials, such as wood, marble, and metal, to find a configuration that best matched the Palazzo Reale, eventually settling on a sophisticated yet aggressive conical shape for the table. The throne itself was designed to be low and wide, allowing for backlighting, and were designed to emphasize Amidala's costume's unique silhouette,<ref name="Art of TPM" /> and all of the furniture pieces in the throne room were set dressing for the film.<ref name="Galactic Backpacking 2" />

For the exterior of the palace, the design had to enhance the natural landscape surrounding it, rather than mar it, so as to symbolize Naboo philosophy. Part of the solution was found in the dome-covered, aqueduct-like complex of the [[Wikipedia:Marin County Civic Center|Marin County Civic Center]] in the hills above [[California]]'s portion of [[Wikipedia:U.S. Route 101|U.S. Route 101]]. Further inspiration was drawn from the [[Wikipedia:Blue Mosque, Istanbul|Blue Mosque]] in [[Wikipedia:Istanbul|Istanbul]], [[Wikipedia:Turkey|Turkey]], for its multi-sized domes and six minarets along with its sense of symmetry; these inspirations were mixed with [[Wikipedia:Venice|Venetian]] architecture to create the overall look of the palace exterior.<ref name="Art of TPM" />

===Filming and post-production for ''The Phantom Menace''===
{{Quote|We have a matte painting of, uh, Theed city to put back there, and the light fixtures on the wall in the hallway, uh, are, uh, not what George wants, so we're gonna replace them with something else.|[[John Knoll]], Visual Effects Supervisor for ''The Phantom Menace|<ref name="The Beginning">''[[Star Wars: The Making of Episode I The Phantom Menace]]''</ref>}}
[[File:TheedPalace-FilmingNeimoidians.png|thumb|right|300px|Filming of the scene with Sidious, Gunray, and Haako in the Palazzo Reale]]
The scene featuring Amidala being escorted by Gunray and Haako down the Royal Staircase was filmed on the Palazzo Reale's Honour Grand Staircase. Editing and camera work was used to hide the lion statues at the bottom of the stairs. At the top of the staircase is the passageway where the conversation between Gunray, Haako, and the hologram of Darth Sidious was filmed, and behind the camera during that shot is the location of the throne room.<ref name="Galactic Backpacking 2" /> Lucas was unsatisfied with the light fixtures in one of the hallways in the palace, so they were replaced for the final version of the film. The archways of the palace leading outside were filled digitally with tanks and battle droids or with a matte painting.<ref name="The Beginning" />
